question: Why is food hygiene particularly critical in healthcare settings according to the text?

options.A: Patients have higher financial resources to pay for meals
options.B: Vulnerable patients with compromised immune systems are more susceptible to foodborne illnesses
options.C: Hospital kitchens are exempt from standard public health laws
options.D: Foodborne pathogens cannot survive in clinical environments

explanation: Patients in healthcare settings often have weakened immune systems, making them much more vulnerable to severe complications from foodborne illnesses. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T006#GNS227_U7_T006_h1)

question: What is the primary goal of implementing proper food hygiene and safety measures?

options.A: To ensure the safety and wholesomeness of food from production to consumption
options.B: To increase the commercial profitability of food vendors
options.C: To completely eliminate the need for clinical nutritionists
options.D: To accelerate the expiration date of perishable food items

explanation: Food hygiene encompasses all conditions and measures necessary to ensure the safety and wholesomeness of food throughout its lifecycle. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T006#GNS227_U7_T006_h1)

question: Who is classified as a food handler according to the text?

options.A: Only the chief executive officer of a food manufacturing company
options.B: Anyone who directly touches food, equipment, utensils, or packaging during preparation, service, or storage
options.C: Patients who consume meals in a hospital ward
options.D: Regulatory inspectors who visit food establishments annually

explanation: A food handler is defined as anyone who directly touches food, equipment, utensils, or packaging at any stage of food handling. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T006#GNS227_U7_T006_h2)

question: What should a food handler do immediately if they develop a personal illness or skin infection?

options.A: Continue working while wearing double gloves
options.B: Ignore the symptoms if they seem mild
options.C: Immediately report the illness or infection to their supervisor
options.D: Take over-the-counter medication and avoid telling anyone

explanation: Food handlers have a direct responsibility to immediately report personal illnesses or skin infections to their supervisors to prevent contaminating food. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T006#GNS227_U7_T006_h2)

question: What temperature range is specifically referred to as the 'danger zone' where bacteria multiply rapidly?
explanation: Bacteria often multiply rapidly in the danger zone of temperatures between 5°C and 60°C. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T006#GNS227_U7_T006_h3)

question: What is a primary mechanism of cross-contamination in food preparation?

options.A: Storing dry grains in airtight plastic containers
options.B: Washing raw vegetables with potable running water
options.C: Transferring pathogens from raw meat to ready-to-eat foods via unwashed cutting boards or hands
options.D: Cooking poultry to an internal temperature above 75°C

explanation: Cross-contamination occurs when pathogens transfer from raw foods to ready-to-eat foods via unwashed utensils, cutting boards, or hands. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T006#GNS227_U7_T006_h3)

question: What is considered the single most effective intervention for preventing the spread of pathogens by food handlers?

options.C: Rigorous and frequent hand washing with soap and running water
options.D: Using scented hand lotions before handling food

explanation: Rigorous hand hygiene using soap and running water is the single most effective intervention to stop pathogen transmission. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T006#GNS227_U7_T006_h4)

question: Which of the following conditions requires a food handler to be immediately excluded from food duties?
explanation: Food handlers suffering from gastrointestinal symptoms like diarrhea and vomiting must be immediately excluded from food handling until they recover. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T006#GNS227_U7_T006_h4)

question: What does the FIFO inventory method stand for and achieve in food storage?

options.A: First-In, First-Out; ensures older stock is used first to minimize spoilage
options.B: Fast-In, Fast-Out; speeds up food preparation times
options.C: Frozen-In, Fresh-Out; maximizes refrigerator energy efficiency
options.D: Flavor-In, Flavor-Out; enhances the taste of preserved meals

explanation: FIFO stands for First-In, First-Out, ensuring older inventory is utilized before newer items to prevent spoilage. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T006#GNS227_U7_T006_h5)

question: What is an unsafe method for defrosting frozen perishable foods?

options.B: Defrosting under cold running potable water
options.C: Defrosting on a kitchen counter at room temperature
options.D: Defrosting inside a microwave as part of immediate cooking

explanation: Defrosting on a counter at room temperature allows food to enter the danger zone where bacteria multiply rapidly, making it unsafe. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T006#GNS227_U7_T006_h5)

question: What is the difference between cleaning and sanitization in food establishments?

options.A: Cleaning uses chemicals while sanitization uses only plain water
options.B: Cleaning removes visible dirt and grease, whereas sanitization reduces microorganisms to safe levels
options.C: Cleaning is done daily while sanitization is done once a year
options.D: Cleaning is for floors only, while sanitization is exclusively for food

explanation: Cleaning removes visible dirt and food residues, while sanitization reduces the number of harmful microorganisms to safe public health levels. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T006#GNS227_U7_T006_h6)

question: What does an Integrated Pest Management (IPM) approach primarily rely on?

options.A: Leaving food waste exposed overnight to trap pests
options.B: Environmental sanitation, sealing entry points, proper waste management, and safe pest control methods
options.C: Using high-toxicity pesticides directly on food preparation surfaces
options.D: Ignoring small rodents as they do not carry pathogens

explanation: IPM combines sanitation, sealing entry points, proper waste disposal, and safe control measures to manage pests effectively without contaminating food. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T006#GNS227_U7_T006_h6)

question: Which Nigerian agency is prominently involved in regulating food safety standards alongside local health authorities?

options.A: National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (NAFDAC)

explanation: NAFDAC is a key regulatory body establishing guidelines and oversight for food safety and standards in Nigeria. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T006#GNS227_U7_T006_h7)

question: What is a mandatory legal requirement for individuals working as food handlers in public establishments in Nigeria?

options.A: Possessing a university degree in culinary arts
options.B: Undergoing mandatory medical fitness screenings and obtaining health certification
options.C: Owning a commercial vehicle for food delivery
options.D: Submitting a monthly financial audit report

explanation: Food handlers must undergo mandatory medical fitness screening and obtain certification or health permits to prove they are free from infectious diseases. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T006#GNS227_U7_T006_h7)

question: Why is it important to use practical demonstrations and visual aids in food handler training?

options.A: To make the training session take as long as possible
options.B: To accommodate varied literacy levels and make concepts engaging and clear
options.C: To replace the need for professional sanitation equipment
options.D: To ensure food handlers never have to wash their hands again

explanation: Food handlers have varied literacy levels, so visual aids and practical demonstrations help ensure concepts are clearly understood and retained. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T006#GNS227_U7_T006_h8)

question: What is the recommended approach regarding the frequency of food handler education?

options.A: Training should only occur once during the initial job interview
options.B: Training must be a continuous process reinforced by refresher courses and supervision
options.C: Training is unnecessary if the employee has cooked at home before
options.D: Training should only happen after a major food poisoning outbreak occurs

explanation: Training should not be a one-time event; it must be continuously reinforced through refresher courses and ongoing supportive supervision. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T006#GNS227_U7_T006_h8)
